To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel reinforcement learning framework for query object localization and demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework on three different datasets.
(1) We propose a novel approach to query object localisation, where an agent is trained on a small exemplary set to localise objects of interest.

1) we learn transferable reward for query object localization, which enables test-time policy adaption to new environments where reward signal is not readily available; 2) we learn transferability across different tasks by using the transferable reward signal, which can be used to repurpose the trained agent from a specific class to another one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning a transferable reward function that can be adapted to a novel environment at test time for reinforcement learning.
the development and evaluation of methods for the localization of objects of interest in images.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is able to learn a transferable policy that adapts to new environments and can also be reused to solve new tasks.
we learn a transferable policy to query objects of interest specified in a small exemplary set, and we show the effectiveness of our proposed method on corrupted MNIST and CU-Birds datasets.
our method outperforms fine tuning approaches and achieves state-of-the-art performance in query object localization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are the first to study query object localization from an agent’s perspective, which is different from the existing methods in that we do not require the agent to be provided with any supervision signal during testing.

we learn a reward signal that is transferable across different tasks, environments, and classes, which allows us to train a policy that can be adapted to new environments and classes without retraining.

our approach enables the agent to learn a policy for object query localization in a way that it can be easily transferred across different environments, and the agent is able to adapt to new environments with minimal additional data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learning transferable reward can enable a policy to adapt to unseen test environments and generalize to unseen object classes.
learning an appropriate reward signal can be crucial for learning a transferable agent.
the reward signal can be learned from a set of examples and used to adapt a policy to unseen environments.
